interfaces.name: text
interfaces.constraints: Unicode Python string; empty input allowed. No coercion of missing values, case folding, normalization, transliteration, stemming or deletion. Caller resolves table missing-value policies before this operation.

interfaces.name: word_characters
interfaces.constraints: Explicit string whose code points form the word-run alphabet. Empty and repeated characters allowed; membership only matters. Must be disjoint from whitespace_characters. Caller preserves the same policy across training and inference and chooses it for the intended domain.

interfaces.name: whitespace_characters
interfaces.constraints: Explicit string whose code points form the whitespace-run alphabet. Empty and repeated characters allowed. No automatic Unicode whitespace expansion. Must be disjoint from word_characters; characters outside both alphabets become individual tokens.

interfaces.name: result
interfaces.constraints: Ordered list of nonempty string tokens; empty input returns an empty list. Consecutive word or whitespace code points form runs; all other code points are individual tokens. Joining tokens exactly reproduces the input. Code-point semantics are not grapheme or linguistic segmentation. Independent chunk tokenization may change run boundaries. Witness metadata gives bounds only, not an exact token-array shape.

providers.operation: Split text into maximal caller-defined word and whitespace runs and individual remaining code points without changing text.
providers.plain_description: Split text into pieces using caller-chosen character groups, preserving every character.

limitations: Automated Tier 3 only; no human Tier 1 review or Tier 2 usage certification.
Caller supplies disjoint word and whitespace alphabets and preserves policy across training and inference. Domain-specific language and sequence semantics are not inferred.

Lossless code-point segmentation only; no Unicode normalization, grapheme handling, stemming, transliteration, whitespace deletion or linguistic word detection. Independent chunks can change run boundaries.
Witness output contains token-count bounds, not exact token shape or observed text. Downstream witnesses must handle variable-length sequences explicitly.

Connected feature parity uses an explicit source character-policy adapter, diagnostic source feature loaders and synthetic inputs. It does not certify new-domain predictive accuracy or historical-runtime equivalence.
Installed files match their own RECORD hashes and active dependency constraints. Independent package provenance, clean deployment and other platforms are not certified.
This review qualifies one generic tokenizer atom, not the application-specific text-cleaning policy, full feature pipeline or original competition CDG.
